key_insight: Grain-boundary segregation in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni delays the onset of plastic flow by slowing early deformation, mainly through chemistry-driven effects at the boundaries.
engineering_relevance: Tuning grain-boundary chemistry in nanocrystalline stainless steels could improve strength and delay yielding under load without changing dislocation mechanisms.
method: Hybrid MD/MC simulations on three independent nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni polycrystals
Compared segregated, annealed, and random controls on identical microstructures
Evaluated response under constant stress and fixed strain-rate loading across multiple temperatures
evidence_signal: Under 4.6 GPa at 300 K, segregated polycrystals reached 50% strain about 16% later than random ones, and at fixed strain rate they showed a 6-7% higher peak stress than annealed controls across 300, 750, and 950 K.
watch_item: The apparent Cr/Ni segregation depends on the chosen reference region, so compositional conclusions must be interpreted carefully when comparing grain interior and boundary shells.
paper_title: Grain-boundary segregation delays the onset of plastic flow in nanocrystalline Fe-18Cr-12Ni
